name_collision.verdict: There is NO single product called 'Phone MCP'. Five exact/near-exact name matches; the advertised product the owner saw CANNOT be pinned down from the description alone (no ad creative/timeframe/channel supplied).
exact_matches: premex-phone-mcp (app-store exact name; data tools only, no UI control)
agi-agentic-phone-mcp (marketed as the ad genre suggests; not named Phone MCP)
viandwi24-phone-mcp (architecturally the fleet's shape; no marketing found)

background_taxonomy.A: Service stays connected while screen is off (foreground service + battery exemption; tools wake screen on demand). Credential lock still blocks control. Systems: viandwi24, Premex, PhonePi, htekdev, ScreenMCP.
background_taxonomy.B: Agent works on a hidden second display (VirtualDisplay) while the user uses the main screen — the ONLY true concurrent background found. Systems: Mika only.
background_taxonomy.C: Marketing 'background' = foreground mirroring/automation, unattended or physical screen dark; agent and user fight over one display if the phone is picked up. Systems: mobile-mcp, Android-MCP, DroidMind, scrcpy family, AGI, Melaya, Mobilerun Portal, Open-AutoGLM.

hard_limits_no_bypass_found: biometric/CAPTCHA hand-off — every credible project hands these back to the human
pattern_split: Field splits into (i) host-side ADB/Xcode servers (host must be present), (ii) phone-as-toolbox servers (on-device direct APIs; no UI control), (iii) on-device UI agents (Accessibility ± MediaProjection ± shell helper, outbound broker/cloud connection; only group that works away from a host).
architecture_verdict_for_this_builder: On-device agent + remote orchestration matches the strongest pattern in the field (viandwi24 topology; Mika execution model; Melaya policy model). Differentiated stack: thin Kotlin agent (ForegroundService + Accessibility; shell helper via wireless-debugging pairing ONLY if virtual-display concurrency or shell-level ops are truly needed) -> outbound WSS to a broker with per-device identity -> snapshot-first MCP tools with on-device policy enforcement and phone-only approval for gated actions -> orchestrator-side planning with screenshot fallback. NOT worth building: another ADB host server (commoditised), a proprietary cloud relay before the local/self-host path is solid, any iOS UI-control promise.
token_offload_finding: Observation cost is the builder's token lever: compact snapshot-with-refs (viandwi24: one line per meaningful node, [n12] refs, 300-line/~12KB cap, stale-ref errors) beats screenshot-per-step on cost, latency AND leakage; a UI tree is cheaper and less leaky than screenshots; screenshots reserved for canvas/video/custom-drawn surfaces. Screenshots and UI trees are sent to the model provider in every vision/tree system — 'local-first' describes transport, not inference.
copy_patterns: viandwi24 topology hardened (one persistent outbound WS; thin MCP shim next to orchestrator; reqId-correlated commands with timeouts)
intent/deep-link first, node actions before coordinate taps, gestures last
Melaya-grade policy: allowlist double-enforced (broker + on-device vs actual foreground package), HITL gates the remote caller cannot satisfy, phone-only approval (Mika rule)
Mika virtual-display path only if true concurrency is a requirement; foreground mode default/fallback
DroidMind-style guardrails on any shell escape hatch (named parameterised ops first; allowlist + risk tiers + audit log)
honest lock/FLAG_SECURE semantics (wake-on-demand, swipe/none locks only, hard-fail to human on credential locks)
survival engineering for cheap OEM phones (typed FGS, battery exemption, reconnect/backoff/heartbeat, honest boot-recovery story, Accessibility takeScreenshot over MediaProjection for stills)
traps: believing 'background' marketing (Accessibility/ADB drive the foreground display)
Google Play distribution for an autonomous Accessibility agent (Play policy bars it; plan sideload/direct distribution)
single shared token / cleartext transport (one leak = full phone compromise, no selective revocation)
raw shell + an LLM that reads screens = prompt-injection RCE on a signed-in phone
MediaProjection as screenshot foundation (per-session consent, auto-stop on lock, OEM variance)
screenshot-first perception on low-end hardware (slow, expensive, leakiest)
assuming the helper survives (wireless debugging self-disables; OEM task killers; heartbeat + degraded-mode reporting beats silent failure)
one phone = one session (fleet scale = more physical phones)
benchmark/marketing reliability claims (AndroidWorld reference agent: 30.6% vs 80% human — design for supervised, resumable, step-verified tasks)
iOS as a roadmap checkbox (no on-device background-control path exists)
calibration: AndroidWorld (Google DeepMind, ICLR 2025): best agent 30.6% of 116 tasks vs 80% human. Any vendor claiming near-human phone autonomy is claiming to beat that benchmark.
